purpose: Candidate persona fields for context mapping, selected by enterprise, article, or product tags.

priority_definitions.primary: Review first: the field describes a closely related preference, attitude, or way of processing information.
priority_definitions.supporting: Optional background context with a less direct relationship to the tag.

status_definitions.mapped: One or more candidate fields are available, subject to the stated limitations.
status_definitions.no_available_field: No sufficiently specific link is proposed within the current 70-field subset.
status_definitions.campaign_metadata: The tag expresses campaign intent, not evidence about the individual.

interpretation_rules: Links are project-authored relevance hypotheses, not validated causal relationships.
Priority concerns context selection, not recommendation scores or action probabilities.
No link specifies whether a persona will like, dislike, comment, buy, or not buy.
Use only valid values actually available for the individual; do not impute missing fields or pad a context to 15 fields.
Retain original enum strings. The string None is a valid value where declared, not a missing value.
A tag ID and a persona field ID belong to separate namespaces, even when both are topic_coffee.
Enterprise tags describe public organization or brand context; they do not establish that an agent knows, trusts, or prefers the enterprise.
Multiple tags may refer to the same field. Deduplicate fields when assembling context; repeated links are not independent evidence.
This file does not implement per-persona top-15 ranking, prompt assembly, or recommendation policy.
Do not pass these fields again to emotion or action steps merely because they appear in this mapping.
Customer testimonials inside an article are distinct from other agents' comments, which remain unavailable to the agent.

limitations: The current persona subset has no sufficiently specific field for preference toward local enterprises.
The current persona subset has no sufficiently specific field for preference toward chain businesses.
